messages:
sara: Quick thought: instead of big manifests or tiny headers, what about a reservation token handshake so loaders can claim chunks before reading? helps avoid mid-read evictions/race.
henry: Explain briefly? Token sounds like lease, but who mints it and how do we avoid extra roundtrips?
sara: Flow idea: client asks local cache manager for chunk X. If cache miss, cache manager requests a reservation token from the origin (or directory service). Origin returns token + small proof (checksum + generation id). Cache then streams chunk; token prevents origin from garbage-collecting or moving chunk until token TTL.
oliver: TTLs are tricky across networks. If token expires mid-read, we need a revocation or renewal path. Also origin might be S3-like where you can't lock objects.
maya: Could implement as soft reservation: origin records the token in a lightweight registry (Dynamo/consul) and GC only removes objects older than last-token-time + grace. Not perfect but reduces races.
sara: Right — goal isn't strict locking but to reduce the window where a chunk gets compacted away during a hot startup. We accept eventual consistency but want to prevent the common case of GC causing read failure.
henry: How this compares to having a micro-header with chunk checksums at front of shard? That lets readers validate slices without reservation.
sara: Micro-header + reservation is complementary. Header validates content; reservation reduces supply-side churn while a sequence of chunks is being prefetched/warmed. Both together reduce fault and validation traffic.
oliver: API sketch for cache manager:
`ReserveToken reserve_chunk(shard_id, chunk_idx, budget_ms)`
`ReleaseToken(reserve_token)`
`ReadChunk(reserve_token) -> bytes | Raise Fallback`
henry: Nice. Budget_ms lets caller decide fast-fail if too slow. If reserve fails, caller can opt for streaming fallback.
maya: Telemetry to add: reserve_success_rate, avg_reserve_latency, reserve_ttl_renewals, chunk_revocations. Also record whether reservation prevented a GC-induced miss.
sara: Failure modes: token minted but consumer crashes -> leak tokens. Need automated eviction and conservative GC. Make tokens cheap and TTL'd and include origin-side counters to ignore stale tokens after generation bump.
oliver: Security/privacy: tokens should not leak model provenance. Use opaque IDs signed by origin key so local registries can verify authenticity without exposing internal paths.
henry: For Private deploys, token issuance can be behind KMS auth and role checks. For hosted, we can allow public tokens with short TTL.
maya: Perf concern: extra RTT for reservation. Mitigation: pipelined reservation+header fetch in same request to origin. Origin responds with token and header blob in one response. That keeps one RTT.
sara: Good. We should also allow a fast-path: origin responds with token=0 and header if it knows it's safe (e.g., object pinned), meaning no soft reservation needed.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: experiment kickoff: reservation-probe v1 on canary pool (tag: canary/reservation-2026-03-21).
oliver: Tests: simulate aggressive GC while multiple clients reserve and read. Ensure no observed half-applied-layer states and model checksums still validate. Also test token expiry during long reads and ensure fallback is correct.
henry: Rollback gates: if reserve_failure_rate > 2% or cold-start P95 increases by >15% we disable reservation probe. Also require no increase in checksum failures.
maya: Implementation note: registry should be eventual-consistent and sharded by model namespace. Keep footprint tiny to avoid cost. Maybe a compact bloom-ish bitmap per shard to note active chunk ranges.
sara: I'll draft an RFC addendum: handshake sequence diagrams, API, header+token combined spec, telemetry, test matrix and canary rollback thresholds. Will ping infra and security for registry sizing and auth model.
oliver: Thanks — add a short compatibility section for safetensors vs monolithic bin formats. Reservation should be format-agnostic as long as chunk offsets are known.
sara: Agreed. Draft by tomorrow EOD. Thanks all. :rocket:
